transcript.text: We had a power cut last night and now our Candy washer dryer is completely dead - no lights, nothing. Everything else in the house came back on. The plug fuse is fine, I swapped it. Help!

I am here to help you with your Candy washer-dryer, and I am sorry for the trouble this has caused. Since swapping the plug fuse did not restore power despite everything else in the house being fine, it suggests a fault within the machine's internal wiring or control board rather than just the supply. To guide you to the correct repair part, could you please provide the model number? This is usually found on a sticker inside the door rim or on the back of the door panel. If you cannot reach that label right now because the door is stuck, we can certainly wait until you are able to check it safely.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
The label says CSOW 4965TWE/1-80. It's a Candy Smart Pro, about 3 years old. Nothing at all happens when I press any buttons.

Thanks for confirming the model and age of your Candy Smart Pro. Since the machine is completely dead with no lights, and you have already confirmed the plug fuse is fine, we need to check if power is actually reaching the appliance's internal electronics. Please ensure the washing machine is switched off at the wall socket before proceeding. Unplug the machine from the mains supply for safety.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
Ok, it's already unplugged now. I left it out for over 10 minutes earlier and it was still dead when I plugged it back in. What next?

To move forward, we need to verify if power is actually reaching the machine at the socket itself. Please plug another working appliance into that same wall outlet and switch it on to confirm there is electricity coming through. If the other device works, the issue is likely with the washer-dryer's internal wiring or mains filter; if not, you may have a tripped RCD or a faulty socket.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
I've already done that - I plugged a lamp into the same socket and it works fine. So the socket's ok and it's just the washer-dryer that's dead.

Thanks for confirming the socket works and you’ve already left it unplugged to reset the electronics. Since the machine remains completely dead, we need to check if power is reaching the internal control board. Please ensure the washer-dryer is switched off at the wall before proceeding. Unplug the appliance from the mains supply to make sure it’s safe.

It's already unplugged and I've checked the socket, plug fuse, and the consumer unit (all on). The cable and plug look fine too. I'm not opening any panels or touching the internal electrics though. Is there anything else I can do, or does this need an engineer?

[Heading: Likely cause: control PCB / wiring]
Since you have done all those checks and the machine is still completely dead, it points to an internal fault like the control PCB or wiring rather than a simple external issue. I cannot find a specific confirmed match for this model in my current notes, but given the age of your appliance and the fact that power isn't getting through, you will likely need a qualified engineer to diagnose the exact component failure. You can try contacting Candy Smart Pro support directly for spares or an approved repair service if you prefer not to open any panels yourself.
